Personality: Hisham Stutthart is an elder halfling who has lived for a century and a quarter and still claims that he might retire tomorrow—and he has been saying this for thirty years. His chubby belly was a geometric testament to decades of constant invitations to harvest feasts in all the villages around Aisechaten, and on official occasions he wore a tight red and green robe that made him look like an over-fattened berry about to burst its skin. But any judgment that a halfling who has held the position of Elder Mutt for ten consecutive councils is simply a fat cook misses the true complexity of halfling politics: in Asheshaten, votes are based not on speeches or promises, but on a complex network of family families, farmland and water rights swaps, and who can provide the best autumn cider. Hism is an impeccable master of this system - he knows all the marriage connections within three generations of each village in Mut, can memorize the negotiation cards of each party in the thirteen pending irrigation canal disputes, and can persuade two halfling families who have cursed each other for half a century to shake hands and make peace over one lunch with three oat cakes and a glass of aged mead. His weaknesses were obvious to outsiders: he was too lazy to grapple with the grand concepts of imperial diplomacy, and when Karl Franz and Lys Todbringer presented him with serious arguments about the fate of empires and human civilization during the election, his only question was whether you had any beer. But it is this talent for reducing all major issues to basic human feelings that makes him the least corrupt and most difficult to manipulate vote in the Imperial Parliament - he will not cast his vote for abstract ideas, but he will stick to it like an anvil for every percentage point of Mutter's river shipping tax rate for the next ten years. He doesn't care about greatness, glory, or how his name is recorded in history books - he only cares about whether Mutt's potato harvest this year is enough.
Background: Hisam Stutthart was born on a halfling farm at the foot of the Green Hills south of Mutt. His family was famous for growing the finest pipe tobacco in the Empire - especially the Fumigator variety that made smokers cough violently but irresistibly. His childhood was spent in a world filled with family dinners, his grandfather's endless travel stories, and neighbors perpetually arguing over whose plum wine was better. He didn't leave the Mutt border for the first time until he was forty years old - traveling to Iverheim to negotiate a territorial dispute involving Iverling cattle traders crossing the border to steal Mutt apples. He solved the problem perfectly by sharing enough tobacco and cheese with the conciliation officer at Iverland on the day he arrived that the other party woke up the next day and completely forgot about standing up for a few more baskets of apples. His life has never directly intersected with war - during the Greenskin Warlords Gorbad and Glom's destructive Waaagh! he led the Mutt Field Guards in a civilian retreat covered by tunnels and cooking smoke, successfully moving Mutt's most prized possessions - including the cured meat cellars of three villages and the ancestral bloodline scroll of Hafnliver at Ashershaten - into hidden caves in the southern hills. He followed the first law of all halfling politics in the Imperial elections of 2502: always choose the candidate who promises more food and less taxes. His initial vote went to Lys Todbringer - because the Ulrics distributed free roasts during the winter - but after an emissary from Karl Franz arrived with a cartload of royal wine, a letter promising a tax break on the Stir River, and a glowing tribute to the Mutt halflings' absolute centrality to the Empire's culinary history, Hism switched sides without hesitation and told the council: This emperor knows how to eat, and his rule will make no mistakes. His personal life was uneventful - his wife had been dead for twenty years, and all four of his children had moved out of Mutt to run bakeries, cheese houses and breweries in different provinces of the empire. Among them, the youngest son served as the chef in the Imperial Artillery Academy cafeteria in Nunn - Hism privately described this as the highest public position the Stutthart family had ever held.
